Infrastructure as Code with Pulumi on AWS

A public Nginx web container and an S3 static website, written in Python, deployed and then destroyed by Pulumi, with the state stored in a remote S3 backend.

◎Goal & architecture

Describe the infrastructure in a Python program, let Pulumi compute the plan and create the resources on AWS, check that they work, then delete everything.

Pulumi CLI v3.274.1Python 3.14pulumi-aws 7.54.0 AWS CLI 2.36.8Region eu-north-1ECS Fargate · ALB · S3

1AWS account setup

We create a dedicated IAM user (helmidev03) with an access key used only by the CLI, configured with aws configure. The keys stay in ~/.aws/credentials and never appear in the code.

2Remote state backend

Pulumi records the list of resources it created in a state file. Instead of keeping it on the PC, we store it in a dedicated S3 bucket that the whole group can share:

  • private: Block Public Access enabled;
  • encrypted: SSE-S3 (AES-256);
  • versioned: every version of the state is kept, so we can roll back.
S3 backend + pulumi login

4The infrastructure code

Everything is described in __main__.py. Each Python object maps to one AWS resource:

ResourceRole
SecurityGroupFirewall: port 80 open to the Internet
LoadBalancer · TargetGroup · ListenerFixed public address that forwards HTTP :80 traffic to the container
ECS Cluster · TaskDefinition · ServiceRuns 1 nginx container on Fargate and keeps it running (0.25 vCPU, 512 MB)
S3 Bucket · BucketWebsiteConfigurationBucket in static website mode (index.html, error.html)
BucketPublicAccessBlock · BucketPolicyAllows public read only (s3:GetObject)
BucketObjectv2 ×3Uploads the files from the www/ folder

Outputs: nginx_url, site_url and site_bucket.

Show the full code (__main__.py)
tp3-iac/__main__.py
"""TP3 - IaC with Pulumi (AWS, Python)
1) An Nginx web container on ECS Fargate, exposed publicly through a Load Balancer (port 80)
2) An S3 bucket configured to host a static website
"""
import json
import mimetypes
import os

import pulumi
import pulumi_aws as aws

# ───────────────────────── Network (default VPC) ─────────────────────────
vpc = aws.ec2.get_vpc(default=True)
subnets = aws.ec2.get_subnets(filters=[{"name": "vpc-id", "values": [vpc.id]}])

# Firewall: open port 80 (HTTP) to the whole Internet
web_sg = aws.ec2.SecurityGroup(
    "web-sg",
    vpc_id=vpc.id,
    description="HTTP public (port 80)",
    ingress=[{"protocol": "tcp", "from_port": 80, "to_port": 80, "cidr_blocks": ["0.0.0.0/0"]}],
    egress=[{"protocol": "-1", "from_port": 0, "to_port": 0, "cidr_blocks": ["0.0.0.0/0"]}],
)

# ───────────────────────── 1. Nginx container ─────────────────────────
# Public Load Balancer = fixed address reachable from the Internet
alb = aws.lb.LoadBalancer(
    "nginx-alb",
    load_balancer_type="application",
    security_groups=[web_sg.id],
    subnets=subnets.ids,
)
target_group = aws.lb.TargetGroup(
    "nginx-tg",
    port=80,
    protocol="HTTP",
    target_type="ip",
    vpc_id=vpc.id,
    health_check={"path": "/"},
)
listener = aws.lb.Listener(
    "http-listener",
    load_balancer_arn=alb.arn,
    port=80,
    default_actions=[{"type": "forward", "target_group_arn": target_group.arn}],
)

# ECS cluster + task definition (official nginx image)
cluster = aws.ecs.Cluster("tp3-cluster")
task = aws.ecs.TaskDefinition(
    "nginx-task",
    family="nginx",
    cpu="256",
    memory="512",
    network_mode="awsvpc",
    requires_compatibilities=["FARGATE"],
    container_definitions=json.dumps([{
        "name": "nginx",
        "image": "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx:latest",
        "essential": True,
        "portMappings": [{"containerPort": 80, "protocol": "tcp"}],
    }]),
)

# Service: keeps 1 container running and registers it behind the Load Balancer
service = aws.ecs.Service(
    "nginx-svc",
    cluster=cluster.arn,
    task_definition=task.arn,
    desired_count=1,
    launch_type="FARGATE",
    network_configuration={
        "subnets": subnets.ids,
        "security_groups": [web_sg.id],
        "assign_public_ip": True,
    },
    load_balancers=[{
        "target_group_arn": target_group.arn,
        "container_name": "nginx",
        "container_port": 80,
    }],
    opts=pulumi.ResourceOptions(depends_on=[listener]),
)

# ───────────────────────── 2. S3 bucket (static website) ─────────────────────────
site_bucket = aws.s3.Bucket("site-bucket", force_destroy=True)

# Allow a public (read-only) bucket policy on THIS bucket
public_access = aws.s3.BucketPublicAccessBlock(
    "site-public-access",
    bucket=site_bucket.id,
    block_public_acls=True,
    ignore_public_acls=True,
    block_public_policy=False,
    restrict_public_buckets=False,
)

# "Static website" mode
website = aws.s3.BucketWebsiteConfiguration(
    "site-website",
    bucket=site_bucket.id,
    index_document={"suffix": "index.html"},
    error_document={"key": "error.html"},
)

# Everyone can READ the files (s3:GetObject), nobody can write
aws.s3.BucketPolicy(
    "site-policy",
    bucket=site_bucket.id,
    policy=site_bucket.arn.apply(lambda arn: json.dumps({
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [{
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Principal": "*",
            "Action": "s3:GetObject",
            "Resource": f"{arn}/*",
        }],
    })),
    opts=pulumi.ResourceOptions(depends_on=[public_access]),
)

# Upload the files from the www/ folder into the bucket
for name in os.listdir("www"):
    aws.s3.BucketObjectv2(
        name,
        bucket=site_bucket.id,
        key=name,
        source=pulumi.FileAsset(os.path.join("www", name)),
        content_type=mimetypes.guess_type(name)[0] or "text/plain",
    )

# ───────────────────────── Outputs ─────────────────────────
pulumi.export("nginx_url", pulumi.Output.concat("http://", alb.dns_name))
pulumi.export("site_bucket", site_bucket.bucket)
pulumi.export("site_url", pulumi.Output.concat("http://", website.website_endpoint))

The resources in the stack have been deleted, but the history and configuration associated with the stack are still maintained.
If you want to remove the stack completely, run `pulumi stack rm dev`.

ResultThe stack has 0 resources: no cluster, Load Balancer or website bucket is left. Only the state bucket remains, with its history, and it costs almost nothing.

★Key takeaways

IaCInfrastructure is code: reproducible, versioned in Git and reviewable by the team.
PulumiA real programming language (Python). preview shows the plan before acting, and up only applies the differences.
Remote stateThe S3 backend shares the state between group members and protects it (private, encrypted, versioned).
Cost controldestroy deletes everything that was created, so no forgotten resource keeps costing money.
